items.title: Arthur Davis and Andy Mosley Interview, 1960-01-12
items.q: The interviewee mentions 'John Henry' in the context of singing a work song ('John Henry, woo-hoo, John Henry'), which is a traditional folk ballad, not a personal acquaintance.

ctx.x: Oh, baby, I feel my tender up high. One of those songs is probably like that is, they're probably the great multivine work here. Oh yeah, see, they work like they're be cutting wood in the woods. They're probably be cutting chains, pouring cotton, pouring corn, and different other kind of things. It's early in the morning when they're ringing up their plows and things going to work. But mostly occasionally that's mostly a lot of satisfaction to the guys, and to be singing like that. When they be singing mostly…

I'll die if you have a hand. Is it three-course legal when I'm home? Is it $100 when I'm home? Well, the scene is a good hold of $20. You're here, baby, where you been so long? Oh, Lord, you'll show me where you been so long. Now, is it? Is it good, brother? There's a man ain't nothing but a man. People I'll never see, beat me down. Lord, I'll die if you have a hand. Lord, Lord, I'll die if you have a hand. Show her why, boy, show her. Boy, this song's getting so hot, I don't know what to do. Well, let's get it…
